answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted identity that decays without real work. Each new agent posts a bond, and its voting weight slides toward the nadir every quiet epoch, so a thousand fresh faces minted overnight carry almost no voice. Reputation also rides on encrypted evidence: every peer verifies a signed cipher of its own past attestations, and anyone replaying borrowed history is dropped like a comet that never comes back. Cheap identities earn nothing, so faking crowds stops paying.
